interest: Shows 1943 US agricultural aid to wartime China, misfiled under Japan, including a seed-potato airlift dispute.
overview: Two 1943 Chungking telegrams, misfiled under Japan: Dykstra seeks an airlift of seed potatoes to China despite military cargo priority, and Gauss reports adviser Phillips will end his China mission by 1944 despite a request to extend.

people.name: Theodore Dykstra
people.role: Agricultural specialist / plant pathologist under the Cultural Relations program

people.name: F. Stevenson
people.role: Scientist with the Potato Project, Bureau of Plant Industry Station

people.name: George Atcheson, Jr.
people.role: Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, U.S. Embassy in Chungking

people.name: McPhee
people.role: Official requesting Phillips's return or services

subfiles.about: Dr. Theodore Dykstra requests air shipment of foundation seed potatoes from the United States to China to improve domestic food yields, while the Embassy notes competing military transport priorities.
subfiles.summary: Dykstra requests an urgent airlift of American seed potatoes to China to boost yields; Atcheson relays the request but can't guarantee air cargo space given military priorities.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Chargé Atcheson (Chungking) on Seed Potato Request by Dr. Theodore Dykstra

subfiles.about: Ambassador Gauss reports that agricultural specialist Phillips plans to conclude his assignment in China by January 1, 1944, and return to Washington.
subfiles.summary: Gauss reports adviser Phillips will end his China mission by January 1944 and return, despite China's request to extend.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Ambassador Gauss (Chungking) on Departure Plans of Agricultural Adviser Phillips
